title: Isolation Sculptor and Temporary Borrowing PRD
creator: Leah Kim
description: PRD to define a combined feature set that lets tenants hold guaranteed capacity while allowing controlled, auditable temporary borrowing of headroom from a shared pool. Focus is on predictable SLA behavior, transparent cost accounting, and safe preemption/eviction semantics for Dedicated clusters.
background: Customers running Redwood Dedicated want the predictability of reserved capacity but also face occasional workload spikes where additional headroom would prevent user-facing degradation. Existing designs either force heavy-handed preemption or unsafe overcommit. We need a model that: (1) keeps committed SLAs intact, (2) allows short-lived borrowing of idle headroom with clear contracts and caps, and (3) provides operators and tenants observability and explicit rollback/fallback paths.
goals: Introduce a tenant-level 'headroom borrow' primitive that allows temporary allocation beyond a tenant's reservation under controlled conditions
Provide preemption semantics and grace windows so borrowers can be safely evicted when capacity becomes scarce
Expose accounting and billing signals for borrowed capacity (metering + tags) to enable chargeback and auditing
Offer an admin API and Console controls to set isolation profiles and borrowing budgets per tenant
Ensure an operator-safe rollout with canary, throttles, and automatic rollback on saturation symptoms
non_goals: Cross-cloud migration of reservations (out of scope for initial launch)
Realtime price auctions between tenants (not a bidding marketplace)
Replacing existing dedicated allocation primitives — this augments current reserved pools
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want to set a per-tenant borrow budget so high-latency spikes don't cause outages for other tenants
As a tenant operator, I want to opt into temporary borrowing so my app can absorb scheduled traffic spikes without complex provisioning
As an SRE, I want clear telemetry and alerts when borrowed headroom exceeds safe thresholds
As a finance manager, I want borrowing events to be visible in billing exports so we can reconcile costs
requirements: Define borrow budget: integer number of vGPU-seconds or token-equivalent units, configurable per-tenant
Borrow events must have metadata: start_ts, end_ts, amount, preemption_deadline, fallback_model (if model variant fallback is possible)
Preemption policy: least-recently-borrowed first, with configurable grace window (default 30s) and hard-evict after grace
Isolation profiles: 'strict', 'lenient', 'buffered' mapping to preemption aggressiveness and probe frequency
Billing signal: borrow_amount and borrow_duration per request/route exported to usage pipeline within 5 minutes
Console: UI to view current borrow consumption, historical trends, and to manually reclaim borrowed headroom
API: Admin endpoints to set budgets, read consumption, and force-reclaim with cause field
Compatibility: no changes required to existing client SDKs for basic behavior; new fields opt-in via admin API only
Observability: traces must include a 'borrowed_headroom' boolean and borrow_id tag for each served request
proposal: Introduce a 'borrow ledger' component in the capacity manager that tracks temporary allocations against a shared pool. Tenants can be granted a borrow budget and an isolation profile. When a request cannot be served from the tenant's reserved allocation but free shared headroom exists, the scheduler will attempt to create a borrow entry and serve request under borrowed units. Borrowed units are tagged in telemetry and billed separately. When cluster pressure rises, the preemption controller will evict borrowed units according to policy, notify affected routes with a brief grace window to fall back to a compatible model or queue for retry.
telemetry_and_success_metrics: Borrow usage rate: borrowed_units_per_hour aggregated per-tenant
SLA preservation: percent of reserved requests served within latency SLO despite borrowing activity
Billing accuracy: percent of borrow events present in billing export within 5 min
Safety alarms: ratio of preemptions with no fallback > 0.1 triggers pager
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): Implement borrow ledger behind feature flag; unit/integration tests + chaos tests in staging
Phase 1 (pilot): Enable for 3 internal tenants and 2 pilot customers with conservative budgets and 'buffered' profile
Phase 2 (gradual): Expand to 20% of clusters; enable console read-only views for customers
Phase 3 (GA): Full API + Console controls, billing integration; default budgets disabled for existing tenants
Rollback criteria: if cluster tail-latency increase > 15% or preemption cascade observed, disable feature flag globally
acceptance_criteria: Borrow ledger persists events reliably across restarts and recovers without double-counting
Preemption controller evicts borrowed units within configured grace windows in 95% of test scenarios
Billing pipeline receives borrow events for pilot customers within 5 minutes in 95% of cases
Console shows live borrow consumption with <10s refresh for pilot clusters
Integration test demonstrating reserved tenant unaffected when another tenant borrows and is later preempted
open_questions: Should borrow budgets be expressed in tokens, vGPU-seconds, or a normalized internal unit? (ops/metering tradeoff)
What is the default isolation profile for new tenants? conservative or permissive?
How should refunds/adjustments be handled for forced preemptions that caused request failures?
Do we expose per-route opt-outs for borrowing (customers may want critical routes never to use borrowed headroom)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Borrowers may starve reserved tenants during simultaneous bursts. Mitigation: strict preemption policy and headroom thresholds + chaos test coverage.
Risk: Billing disputes due to late borrow event propagation. Mitigation: add retries and a reconciliation job exposing mismatches daily.
Risk: Complexity in operator workflows. Mitigation: Provide actionable Console UI and one-click reclaim + recommended guardrail presets.
dependencies: console: new UI panels and reclaim API surface
billing: ingest borrow events and surface in exports
telemetry pipeline: add borrow_id and borrowed_headroom tags
